title: Consistency Training and Circuit Hardening: Does Consistency Training Strengthen the Refusal Feature?

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible with gap: verifying that consistency training strengthens refusal features is useful for understanding the mechanism, but the chain to a new intervention (directly amplifying the refusal feature) is speculative and the original technique already works.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires fine-tuning a model with a consistency training objective, which involves designing the training loop, paired prompt construction, and pre/post probing. Fine-tuning is advanced for beginner CS students with 30 hours.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable: before/after comparison of refusal direction magnitude and geometry. Clean pre-post experimental design with a clear measurable outcome (does the refusal feature get stronger or not).

novelty.reasoning: While the refusal direction is well-established (Arditi et al. 2024, NeurIPS), and methods to harden it exist (ROSI: Rank-One Safety Injection, arXiv:2508.20766), the specific question of whether consistency training as a training objective strengthens the refusal feature's magnitude and geometry has not been directly studied. ROSI injects refusal directions post-hoc without training; the proposed idea instead asks whether a training-time consistency objective naturally amplifies the refusal feature. This is a distinct and novel experimental question. The pre/post SAE-level measurement of refusal feature geometry under consistency training is unexplored territory.
